observations.original_summary: AFN’s own history describes an October 1966 statewide conference and nonprofit incorporation in early 1967. It discusses a coalition of institutions; neither its origin account nor later corporate structures establish a single government for all Alaska Native peoples.

pathways_change.step: Name The Decision And The Seat
pathways_change.text: Separate a public-election goal from a Nation’s own governance process. For the issue you choose, identify the council, school board, agency, legislature or other body with actual authority. Write the decision sought, who is affected and how representatives will report back. Verify current eligibility, deadlines and voting rules through official channels. In Alaska, AFN’s own membership account lists federally recognized tribes, village corporations, regional corporations, and regional nonprofit or Tribal consortium bodies. In your private decision map, identify which institution issued each record and the authority it claims. Do not treat federation membership, corporate shareholding and Tribal citizenship as interchangeable.
pathways_change.verify_added: AFN’s membership account is not a complete inventory of Alaska Native peoples or governments. Verify the relevant Nation’s own account and the specific institution’s public rules before assigning decision-making authority.
pathways_change.scope: Nonpartisan private reading and decision-map preparation. No election eligibility, legal representation, corporate right, Tribal citizenship, consent or current authority is determined.
